items.t: Anheuser-Busch InBev stock: USD 1.5 million Cutwater expansion
sum: On Friday, November 13, AB InBev's US business announced a USD 1.5 million investment to expand production at Cutwater Spirits' main facility in San Diego, California. Global Drinks Intel reported that the funding will support cream-based cocktail production at the 50,000-square-foot site.

The facility houses Cutwater's headquarters, production hub and innovation centre. AB InBev said the project builds on more than USD 5 million in recent investment across the brand's manufacturing network, including facilities in Los Angeles and Baldwinsville, New York.

The expansion targets demand for spirits-based ready-to-drink cocktails and is intended to create new manufacturing opportunities in Southern California. AB InBev also plans to introduce a limited-edition Gingerbread White Russian for the festive season.

Anheuser-Busch's beyond-beer president Jake Kirsch said the investment would support capacity growth for Cutwater and broaden the brand's production footprint. The project adds to AB InBev's efforts to develop businesses beyond traditional beer categories.

sum: Anheuser-Busch InBev reported solid third-quarter growth on Thursday, October 29, while a sharp downturn in China continued to weigh on the brewer's regional mix. The results release, carried by Agence France-Presse, showed organic revenue growth of 4.9% in the quarter and a 22.4% increase in underlying earnings per share.
Anheuser-Busch InBev stock traded at 75.73 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:31 CET on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

Reported revenue rose 9.1% to 16.512 billion US dollars, helped by currency translation. Organic revenue growth reflected a 4.2% increase in revenue per hectoliter, with revenue management and premiumization offsetting broadly stable beer volumes. Total volumes increased 0.4%, as beer volumes slipped 0.1% and non-beer volumes grew 4.0%.

Normalized EBITDA increased 3.9% to 5.957 billion US dollars, but the margin narrowed by 34 basis points to 36.1%. AB InBev attributed the pressure to higher sales and marketing investment and commodity costs, partly offset by overhead discipline. Underlying profit rose to 2.396 billion US dollars from 1.970 billion US dollars a year earlier, while underlying EPS increased to 1.21 US dollars from 0.99 US dollars.

The brewer's growth platforms continued to expand. Revenue from no-alcohol beer rose 35%, Beyond Beer revenue increased 19%, and combined revenue from megabrands grew 7.7%. BEES Marketplace gross merchandise value rose 45% to 1.4 billion US dollars. Management said the company gained or held market share in an estimated two-thirds of its markets and recorded a quarterly volume high in 15 markets.

China was the clear weak spot. Volumes and revenue declined 16.8%, while EBITDA fell 30.5%. AB InBev cited abnormal weather, weak on-premise demand and inventory management in a difficult industry. The company said its performance was below potential, although it saw improvement in the in-home market-share trend, continued growth in premium and core-plus brands, and double-digit growth in online-to-offline sales.

Asia Pacific volumes declined 11.0% and regional revenue fell 9.5%, showing how strongly China affected the quarter. By contrast, Middle Americas revenue grew 12.1% organically, South America 9.1% and EMEA 4.0%, according to the release.

NB, HBM, Nestlé Nigeria, others book N129.4 billion in fees and royalties paid to parent
sum: Seven foreign-owned companies on the Nigerian Exchange that disclose the figures booked N129.4 billion in royalties, licence, technical and management fees to their parent groups in the nine months through September.
That is up 7.7% from N120.1 billion a year earlier, according to their unaudited third-quarter filings.
At three of them — HBM Nigeria, International Breweries and Nigerian Breweries — the fees grew faster than revenue, roughly ten times as fast in International Breweries’ case.
At Nestlé Nigeria, the fees plus interest on a loan from its Swiss parent exceeded the profit left for all shareholders.

The payments are legal and approved by Nigeria’s technology-transfer regulator, NOTAP, which typically caps such fees as a share of net sales. But they land as the subsidiaries emerge from two years of currency losses that wiped out shareholders’ equity at four of them and forced parents to inject fresh capital or forgive loans.

Nestlé Nigeria, 70.81% owned by Switzerland’s Société des Produits Nestlé SA, charged N34.8 billion in general licence fees in the nine months, up from N32.3 billion. It booked another N16.5 billion in shared-service costs from Nestlé Central and West Africa. Together, that is N51.2 billion, or about 5.2% of revenue — the highest ratio in the group.

- On top of that, the company paid N58.5 billion in interest on its intercompany loan, which makes up the bulk of its N426.3 billion of borrowings. Fees and loan interest together came to roughly N110 billion. Profit after tax for all shareholders was N103.4 billion.

Anheuser-Busch InBev stock posts Q3 growth despite China setback
sum: Anheuser-Busch InBev reported stronger third-quarter growth on October 29, 2026, but a sharp setback in China kept pressure on the brewer's regional mix. In its third-quarter results release, the company said organic revenue rose 4.9 percent in the three months ended September 30.

Reported revenue increased 9.1 percent to 16.512 billion US dollars, helped by currency translation. Organic revenue growth reflected a 4.2 percent increase in revenue per hectoliter, as revenue management, premiumization and the Beyond Beer portfolio supported the top line.

Total volumes increased 0.4 percent. Beer volumes declined 0.1 percent, while non-beer volumes rose 4.0 percent. AB InBev said it gained or maintained market share in an estimated two-thirds of its markets and recorded its highest third-quarter volumes in 15 markets, including Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, South Africa, the Dominican Republic and India.

Normalized EBITDA increased 3.9 percent to 5.957 billion US dollars, but the margin contracted by 34 basis points to 36.1 percent. The company attributed the pressure to higher sales and marketing investment and commodity costs, partly offset by disciplined overhead management. Underlying earnings per share rose 22.4 percent to 1.21 US dollars from 0.99 US dollars a year earlier.

China was the clearest drag on the quarter. Revenue and volumes both fell 16.8 percent, while regional Asia Pacific volumes declined 11.0 percent and revenue decreased 9.5 percent. AB InBev cited abnormal weather, weaker on-premise consumption and inventory management. China EBITDA fell 30.5 percent as lower sales created operating deleverage.

Management said the company was making progress in the in-home channel, online-to-offline sales and its core-plus and super-premium brands. It also aims to end 2026 with normal inventory levels in China. That leaves the investment case balanced: pricing and brand mix are supporting growth, but weak Chinese demand and margin investment remain risks to earnings momentum.

AB InBev reaffirmed its 2026 outlook for normalized EBITDA growth of 4 to 8 percent and expects net capital expenditure of 3.5 billion to 4.0 billion US dollars. The company reported nine-month organic revenue growth of 5.4 percent and normalized EBITDA growth of 5.0 percent.

items.t: Learn Why The Bull Case For AB InBev Stock Could Change Following Interim Dividend Announcement
sum: - Anheuser-Busch InBev reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$16,512 million and net income of US$1,597 million, alongside an approved interim dividend of €0.40 per share that was paid on November 23, 2026.

- The combination of higher year on year sales and net income over both the quarter and first nine months, plus a cash dividend aligned with deleveraging goals, highlights how Anheuser-Busch InBev is balancing earnings delivery with capital returns and balance sheet priorities.
- The next step is to consider how this quarterly profitability and interim dividend decision may influence Anheuser-Busch InBev's broader investment narrative.
Scan how Anheuser-Busch InBev's mix of earnings and cash returns compares with other income-focused opportunities by reviewing the hand picked 228 dividend fortresses.

To own Anheuser-Busch InBev, you need to believe its focus on premium brands, emerging markets and digital platforms can keep supporting earnings while it manages mature regions and high debt. The latest quarter showed higher sales and net income versus last year, which helps reinforce that operating thesis rather than changing it.

The near term swing factor still looks like execution in weaker areas such as China and the Beyond Beer portfolio, alongside consumer demand in key emerging markets. The main risk remains that tougher trends coincide with a still leveraged balance sheet, which could limit how much Anheuser-Busch InBev spends on brands and technology.

The interim dividend of €0.40 per share is the announcement that really ties this update together. Management framed it as consistent with financial discipline and deleveraging goals, so income investors are seeing cash returned without an explicit shift toward much heavier capital distributions.

sum: Anheuser-Busch InBev reported stronger third-quarter operating results on Thursday, October 29, while China remained a clear regional weak spot. The brewer's release, carried by AFP, showed organic revenue growth alongside higher underlying earnings.

Organic revenue increased 4.9 percent in the third quarter, while total volumes rose 0.4 percent. Revenue per hectoliter advanced 4.2 percent, supported by revenue management, premiumization and the Beyond Beer portfolio.

Normalized EBITDA grew 3.9 percent to 5.957 billion United States dollars, although the normalized EBITDA margin narrowed by 34 basis points to 36.1 percent. Underlying EPS increased 22.4 percent to 1.21 United States dollars. These are normalized or underlying measures and therefore differ from the company's reported IFRS figures.

Asia Pacific performance remained under pressure. China volumes declined 16.8 percent in the quarter, while regional EBITDA fell 30.5 percent. AB InBev cited inventory management, abnormal weather and continued weakness in the on-premise channel.

The contrast with other markets was material. The company said it delivered record third-quarter volumes in 15 markets, including Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, South Africa, the Dominican Republic and India. Management maintained its full-year outlook for normalized EBITDA growth in line with a medium-term range of 4 to 8 percent.

AB InBev also approved an interim dividend of 0.40 euros per share for fiscal 2026, compared with 0.15 euros for fiscal 2025. A separate SENS disclosure published on November 3 said the company repurchased 214,572 shares between October 26 and October 30 at an average price of 73.1153 euros. The purchases brought total buybacks under the program to 35,358,463 shares, or 1.75 percent of shares outstanding.

Anheuser-Busch InBev stock closed on Xetra at 75.78 euros on Friday, November 6, up 5.40 percent from the 71.90-euro close on Friday, October 30. The weekly advance came as investors weighed broad-based growth and capital returns against weaker Chinese demand and margin pressure.

JTI shares tumbles 20% after Putin seizes control of $4.6B Russian operations
sum: Russian President Vladimir Putin has brought Japan Tobacco International's (JTI) Russian business under state-appointed management, handing control of four local subsidiaries, in which the Japanese tobacco giant has invested $4.6 billion over more than two decades, to a domestic entity.
Under a decree signed by Putin on Thursday, Promyshlennye Aktivy, or Industrial Assets, took over management rights to JTI's stakes in JTI Donskoy Tabak, Petro, JTI Yelets and Kres Neva.
Japan Tobacco Inc., JTI's parent company, confirmed on Friday that the four manufacturing subsidiaries are covered by the measure.

"We are currently reviewing detailed information about this matter, possible responses, and its impact on our group," the company said in a statement, adding that it would promptly disclose any further developments requiring public disclosure.
Japan Tobacco's shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange were down 19.3% on Friday, as heavy sell orders followed news of the Russian takeover, with no shares changing hands.
JTI has operated in Russia since 1999, following Japan Tobacco Inc.'s acquisition of the international business of R.J. Reynolds.
The company became the country's leading tobacco producer by sales volume in 2007 and strengthened its position in 2018 by acquiring Donskoy Tabak.

Meta taps euro market after dollar sale to fund AI push as orders surge
sum: Meta, after $15 billion (about 20 trillion won) in dollar-denominated corporate bonds, has also issued its first-ever euro-denominated bonds as it focuses on raising funds for artificial intelligence (AI) investment.

On the 4th (local time), according to Reuters and Bloomberg, Meta issued €9 billion (about 13.6 trillion won) in corporate bonds in the European bond market. The bonds consist of six tranches with maturities of 4 to 38 years, and the company promised high interest rates about 1.4 times the spread proposed by Alphabet, Google's parent company.

As a result, buy orders poured in totaling €53 billion (about 79.8 trillion won), about six times the issue size. This is the largest order amount ever in the European corporate bond market, surpassing the previous record (€31 billion) set by AB InBev, the world's largest brewer, in 2016. Bloomberg said Meta offered yields high enough to draw in even cautious investors on AI.

Meta also issued $15 billion in dollar-denominated corporate bonds in the United States the previous day. The funds raised in the United States and Europe over two days total about $25 billion (about 34 trillion won).

It is also expanding fundraising through stock issuance. Meta recently conducted a public offering of $25 billion in Class A common stock and $12.5 billion in convertible preferred stock. Adding a program to sell up to $60 billion in Class C nonvoting shares, it is pushing a total of $97.5 billion (about 131 trillion won) in stock issuance.

Behind the large-scale fundraising are surging AI infrastructure investment costs. Meta presented this year's capital expenditures (CapEx) outlook at $135 billion to $145 billion. Third-quarter free cash flow (FCF) recorded a deficit of $2.12 billion.

Global credit rater Standard & Poor's (S&P) kept Meta's credit rating at "AA-" but revised the outlook to "negative" from "stable." The move reflects concern over worsening cash flow and rising financial burdens due to expanded AI investment.

AB InBev sets aside $30 million for unpaid Telangana dues as delayed payments squeeze brewers
sum: Anheuser-Busch InBev has earmarked $30 million for overdue payments from the Telangana government. This situation highlights the challenges in India's controlled alcohol market, characterized by delayed payments. Furthermore, the Telangana government owes nearly $400 million to alcohol companies, prompting industry criticism. United Breweries previously halted supplies due to operating losses and overdue payments in Telangana.
Also read: Govt to meet liquor firms as domestic giants join foreign peers in Scotch dispute
Under the state's system, liquor companies supply products to government-run depots, which then distribute them to retailers, leaving manufacturers dependent on the government for payments.

Telangana is one of India's biggest beer-consuming states by volume. AB InBev chief financial officer Bernardo Novick said the company's total receivables from Telangana had remained relatively stable during the year, but some payments had been outstanding for an extended period.

"We decided to recognise this provision of $30 million," Novick said during the company's earnings call, adding that the brewer was making its best efforts to recover the outstanding amount and protect shareholders.
The company does not expect further meaningful one-off provisions from the situation, Novick said, while cautioning that circumstances could change.

The problem extends beyond AB InBev. United Breweries, which controls about half of India's beer market, had temporarily halted supplies to Telangana Beverages Corporation about a year ago because of operating losses and overdue payments. The brewer had said selling each beer at a loss had made continued operations in the state unsustainable, while substantial delays in payments for supplies to the state corporation had further complicated the situation.

items.t: Campari sales beat estimates but stock slips 5% on US outlook
sum: Investing.com -- Campari Group reported third-quarter sales that exceeded analyst expectations, though shares fell 5.12% on Thursday morning as the company projected a marginal decline in U.S. sales for the full year amid challenging market conditions.

The Italian spirits maker posted third-quarter sales of €777 million, surpassing the analyst consensus of €761.8 million. Organic net sales growth reached 3.4% in the quarter, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of organic growth. For the nine-month period ended September 30, total sales rose 0.4% to €2,289 million, with organic growth of 2.9%.

The company confirmed its full-year outlook for organic net sales growth of approximately 3%, despite ongoing market headwinds. However, Campari now expects a marginal decline in U.S. net sales for the year, even as aperitifs and tequila show strong growth. The weaker performance in some categories and a high comparison base in the fourth quarter are weighing on the North American market, which represents 36% of group sales.

"We have delivered our sixth consecutive quarter of organic net sales growth, while continuing to outperform the industry and gain share in our key markets, thanks to our priority brands," said Chief Executive Officer Simon Hunt.

Europe, accounting for 46% of group sales, delivered 3.4% organic growth, driven by strong performance in Italy and the United Kingdom. Emerging markets posted 9.3% growth, led by Brazil and Argentina. North America grew 1.0%, supported by solid tequila and aperitif sales in the U.S., though the broader portfolio faced pressure.

The company expects organic adjusted EBIT margin expansion for the year, including a €20 million impact from U.S. tariffs. Campari received €15 million in U.S. tariff refunds from 2025, partially reinvested and partially used to offset cost pressures.

WD-40 (WDFC) Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
sum: Shares of household products company WD-40 (NASDAQ:WDFC) jumped 6.8% in the morning session after Northcoast Research initiated coverage on the company with a "Buy" rating and a $265 price target.

An analyst initiation means a new research firm has begun formally tracking the company. Northcoast's "Buy" rating represents a positive first assessment, and its $265 price target suggests it believes the stock has room to grow. New analyst coverage can often bring increased attention to a company from investors. This rating aligns with the broader sentiment from other analysts, who have an average rating of "overweight" and a mean price target of $254.67, according to FactSet.
Is now the time to buy WD-40? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

WD-40's shares are not very volatile and have only had 3 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 14 days ago when the stock gained 2.7% on the news that markets rotated into defensive names following the release of the May CPI report.

The headline 4.2% annual inflation reading spooked the market, but the breakdown matters: energy drove more than 60% of May's monthly price increase, while food at home rose just 0.1% and core inflation came in at only 0.2% for the month. For staples companies whose input costs are food, packaging, and household goods that is a margin reprieve.The World Cup, which kicks off later in the week across U.S., Mexican, and Canadian host cities, added a near-term catalyst. Goldman Sachs has buy ratings on AB InBev, Constellation Brands, and Heineken specifically on tournament beer demand.

WD-40 is up 23.8% since the beginning of the year, and at $243.62 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $252.96 from February 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of WD-40's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $951.90.

Tech giants slump as Nasdaq 100 nears $1 trillion market loss
sum: June 23, 2026 – the Nasdaq 100 index is on track to erase more than $1 trillion in market value as shares of tech giants and chipmakers slump; SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, has fallen below the $2 trillion mark in market capitalization for the first time since its IPO.

SpaceX, which is expected to join the Nasdaq 100, has lost more than $600 billion in value over the last three sessions. Its market capitalization was around $1.95 trillion, assuming the current price pressure persists.
Shares were down 3.6% in premarket trading, while SpaceX remained roughly 9% above the $135 IPO price, as the brisk rally following its IPO last week loses momentum.

Futures on the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 fell 2.5%, signaling a drop of more than 700 points. Analysts estimate the index could shed about $1.15 trillion in market value if the downside momentum persists at around 2.79%.
Chipmakers also took serious losses. Intel fell 6.8%, and Advanced Micro Devices fell 5.2%.

Memory-chip makers, which had been among the brightest growth stars on the S&P 500, are also under pressure: Micron Technology is down 8%, SanDisk down 9.2%, Western Digital down 7.5%. In South Korea, these sectors have also faced significant declines.
Six of the seven in the “Magnificent Seven” – the largest tech companies on Wall Street – are also under pressure amid concerns about higher AI costs.

AB InBev returns to sales growth after three-year lull
sum: AB InBev has posted its first quarterly sales increase in three years, buoyed by growth in premium beer, alcohol-free products and digital sales channels. The brewer also pointed to continued investment in sustainability infrastructure in the UK, including a wastewater treatment facility at its Samlesbury brewery near Preston.

The world’s largest brewer reported revenue growth of 5.8% for the first quarter of 2026, with revenue reaching US$15.27 billion. Beer volumes rose by 1.2% while total volumes were up 0.8%. Underlying earnings per share climbed 20.8% to US$0.97.

Michel Doukeris, chief executive, attributed the performance to what he described as “the strength of the category and the consistent execution of our consumer-centric strategy”. AB InBev gained or maintained market share in 75% of its markets during the quarter.

The brewer said revenue growth was helped by premiumisation and the expansion of its Beyond Beer and no-alcohol portfolios. Revenue from no alcohol beer rose by 27%, while Beyond Beer revenue increased by 37%, as per the company’s figures.
Corona continued to perform strongly outside its domestic market, with revenues rising 16%, while Stella Artois grew 14% and Michelob Ultra 39%.

AB InBev also reported substantial growth through its digital commerce operations. BEES Marketplace gross merchandise value rose by 55% year on year to US$1.1 billion. Total BEES gross merchandise value reached US$14.6 billion during the quarter.
Its direct-to-consumer operations, including Zé Delivery, TaDa Delivery and PerfectDraft, generated US$139 million in revenue and served 12 million active consumers.

AB InBev Q1 Earnings Top on Business Momentum & Solid Organic Revenues
sum: Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV BUD, aka AB InBev, reported first-quarter 2026 results, wherein earnings per share (EPS) and revenues surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Both the top and bottom lines also improved year over year. Bottom-line growth reflected disciplined cost management and positive business momentum, owing to the strength of its diversified footprint and consumer demand for its megabrands.

BUD posted underlying earnings of 97 cents per share, up 20.8% from the year-ago quarter and surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 90 cents by 7.8%. Revenues came in at $15,267 million, up 12% year over year and ahead of the consensus mark of $14,675 million by 4%.
Shares of this Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) company have gained 19.6% in the past three months compared with the industry's 14.4% growth.

BUD's quarter benefited from a combination of revenue management and favorable mix. On an organic basis, revenues rose 5.8%, supported by a 4.5% increase in revenue per hectoliter on continued premiumization.

Execution behind core brands remained a key lever. Combined revenues of its megabrands rose 8.2%, led by Corona, which grew 16% outside of its home market. Management also highlighted strong performances for Stella Artois and Michelob Ultra outside their home markets.

All the brands that have backed out of major festival since Kanye West was booked as the headliner
sum: Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
This year’s Wireless Festival is quickly unraveling after organizers announced disgraced rapper Kanye West as the headliner, prompting multiple brands to withdraw their sponsorship.

West, 48, has faced significant backlash in recent years for making repeated antisemitic remarks. His appearance at London’s annual rap and hip-hop music festival is expected to serve as a major musical comeback, following the release of his new album Bully.

However, the decision to give the Grammy-winning rapper a platform has drawn widespread condemnation from numerous critics, including the Mayor of London and Jewish leaders, who have found his scheduled appearance “deeply troubling.”
Melvin Benn, Managing Director of Wireless Festival organizer Festival Republic, released a statement, acknowledging West’s past remarks as “abhorrent,” but defended booking him as the headliner.

“Forgiveness and giving people a second chance are becoming a lost virtue in this ever-increasing divisive world and I would ask people to reflect on their instant comments of disgust at the likelihood of him performing (as was mine) and offer some forgiveness and hope to him as I have decided to do,” said Benn. “We are not giving him a platform to extol opinion of whatever nature, only to perform the songs that are currently played on the radio stations in our country and the streaming platforms in our country and listened to and enjoyed by millions.”
Still, many of the festival’s sponsors have faced calls to sever ties with the 2026 edition. Here is a list of all the brands that have heeded those calls and backed out.
